commentary: The liquidity hierarchy splits cleanly into three tiers. Nasdaq 100 and NYSE dominate, combining exceptionally low ILLIQ scores (0.0025% and 0.0059% per $1M traded respectively) with deep comparable volumes ($350.9M and $233.0M). Euronext, Tokyo Stock Exchange, and Hong Kong Stock Exchange occupy the mid-pack, each posting ILLIQ below 0.040% per $1M traded and meaningful turnover ratios between 0.4% and 2.8%, though volume tapers sharply to $45.1M or below. The laggard tier—Xetra, SIX Swiss Exchange, Korea Exchange, and London Stock Exchange—shows material degradation. Korea Exchange stands out as notably illiquid at 0.1522% per $1M traded with a 1.5537% AR spread, yet paradoxically maintains a respectable 1.1001% turnover ratio, suggesting concentrated trading in a limited set of names. London Stock Exchange similarly diverges: a poor 0.0815% ILLIQ and 0.8232% spread despite lower turnover (0.5316%), indicating execution costs rise disproportionately to activity. SIX Swiss Exchange presents the opposite profile—tightest AR spread at 0.5292% but middling ILLIQ and minimal $4.0M comparable volume—a signal that spreads compress only at modest scale.
